competences: The learner identifies key facts about local government.
The learner explains information about Roles of the local government using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes local government, local council, district.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about local government.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Roles of the local government.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about local government.
materials: Primary Five SST reference on Roles of the local government
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces local government. They ask "Name the laws that are used at local government." and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about local government
steps.content: Local council II Parish Ward LC II Local council I Village Cell LC I They are all under the National government. The central government is ruled by the president while the local governments are led by chair persons for local council 5. The District level LC V District LC V The county level LC IV Municipality LC IV Sub county level LC III Division LC III This is the government that bears all the major responsibilities towards the people in a country. Differences between the central government and local government Central government Local government There are many local governments. Local council chairperson
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about local government on the chalkboard, including "Local council II Parish Ward LC II; Local council I Village Cell LC I They are all under the National government.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about local government
steps.content: Local government is under the ministry of local government The highest local government unit is LC5 Central government is one government while local government has many local government Central government runs major hospitals while local government controls dispensaries and health centres. Central government builds major roads while local government maintains feeder roads This is a law made by local council. The vice chairperson is responsible for children affairs on the local council1 committee Local election. This is a formal democratic process in which people choose leaders at local council level ie. Local council I -V leaders. The Local government (LC1-LCV).
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about local government on the chalkboard, including "Local government is under the ministry of local government; The highest local government unit is LC5". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about local government
steps.content: Central government is one ▪ Local governments are many. They promote the welfare of children in the society Note: The Vice chairperson is the local council I committee member who is in charge of protection of children’s rights. Decentralization is the transfer of some powers from the central government to the local government.

steps.content: Name the laws that are used at local government. | What are bye laws? | Which ministry runs the affairs of local government? | Who is the current minister of local government? | State any two difference between the Central government and Local government.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Name the laws that are used at local government." and "What are bye laws?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on local government, asks "Name the laws that are used at local government." and follows up with "What are bye laws?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Name the laws that are used at local government." and "What are bye laws?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "What title given to the political head of a district?"
